alert_details.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 19 at 2:38PM PST until November 20 at 3:00AM PST
alert_details.description:
* WHAT...West winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts up to 30 kt and seas
8 to 13 ft.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters from Point Reyes to Pigeon Point
California out to 10 NM.

* WHEN...Until 3 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

alert_details.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 19 at 12:02PM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST
alert_details.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at
favored break points.

* WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

alert_details.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 19 at 12:02PM PST until November 21 at 11:00AM PST
alert_details.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.4 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Franciso Bay and San
Pablo Bay.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM
Friday and 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM
Saturday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The
Pacific Coast will likely be added to the Advisory as early as
Sunday with the San Francisco and San Pablo Bays upgraded to a
Coastal Flood Warning as we approach "King Tides".

sources: Open-Meteo forecast + marine, NOAA CO-OPS tides and water temperature, NWS alerts
